text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- An accused in a fraud case has claimed in a letter to the Judge President Johan Strydom that court officials are allegedly demanding bribes in exchange for destroying case dockets. The case involves eight accused charged with defrauding the government of N$5 million by inflating costs for the construction of the Katutura single quarters.
- The Himba delegation lobbying abroad against the proposed Epupa dam project wrapped up their European tour with a visit to Sweden, which drew extensive media coverage.

- The proposal of a new secret service has found approval in parliament, but some legislators say they are concerned about certain aspects of the draft law, such as the composition of the service and its political neutrality.
- The Zimbabwean government is to clamp down on land ownership by disallowing foreigners to own land and raising agricultural taxes.

- President Sam Nujoma announced that a further 1,000 former People's Liberation Army of Namibia fighters are to be given employment in the special field force. He said over 4,000 job opportunities had been made available for them in government institutions and private companies.
